clue.text: Travelling theatre associated with equestrian activity

parts.note: the Globe is Shakespeare's famous London theatre
trotting is a horse's gait, or the sport of harness racing

explanation.surface: A touring theatre company teams up with a horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Travelling' is the definition, used as an adjective or participle for roving about the world; 'associated with' simply joins the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone forever touring the world's countries is said to be on the move in this fashion.

clue.text: Secure the family line, say, and adopt superior manner

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase before it is to be heard rather than spelt, giving the same sound with different letters

parts.note: to secure a family line you provide yourself with successors, that is, heirs

explanation.surface: Someone ensures the dynasty continues and starts putting on aristocratic manners.
explanation.walkthrough: Providing yourself with heirs secures the line; HEIRS and AIRS sound alike, so the phrase is respelt with AIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting on airs is an idiom for behaving pretentiously, acting grander than one is.

clue.text: Up North, anything involving the French gets the bird

indicators.note: involving means the first word wraps round the second, which sits inside it

parts.note: owt is the dialect word for anything in the north of England
le is the French masculine form of the

explanation.surface: In the north of England, anything to do with the French gets booed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets the bird' looks like an idiom for being jeered, but 'the bird' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A young owl is called this, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Particularly awful English fellow with evidence of debts

parts.note: Greg is a man's name, standing for any fellow
IOUs are written notes acknowledging money owed

explanation.surface: An English chap leaves behind a trail of signed promises to pay, which is shocking.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes something outstandingly bad, shocking in its extent.

clue.text: Revival of clan raised in extremely rough environment

indicators.note: in places the reversed group inside the outer letters
extremely asks for the extremes of rough, its first and last letters
raised in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a clan is a tribe

explanation.surface: A family group is brought back to life after being raised in hard surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means read upwards; 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'rough', and 'in' sets the turned clan between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A renewal or resurgence of something is a new birth for it.

clue.text: Like a roof, perhaps, it's raised and inclined

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: the word it, with 's for is as a link
to be led towards something is to be inclined or disposed to it

explanation.surface: A roof is described as lifted up and sloping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns IT into TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof is often covered with tiles, so 'perhaps' marks it as one example of being so covered.

clue.text: For irritation,' it's spread over joints

indicators.note: spread over means the first word is opened out and laid round the second

parts.note: taken as the letters of its
chines are cuts of meat including the backbone, butchers' joints

explanation.surface: A rash has spread over someone's joints, causing discomfort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' is a link. 'Joints' suggests knees and elbows, but here it means cuts of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Itching is a skin irritation, so this noun names that state.

clue.text: Young relative of eight

parts.note: a descendant two generations below a child has eight ancestors in that generation, being the junior kin of all eight

explanation.surface: A youngster is related to eight people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eight' seems arbitrary or suggests an eight-year-old, but everyone has eight people three generations above them.
explanation.definitionFit: Each person has eight ancestors at that remove, so they are the young descendant of all eight.

clue.text: Plan of presidential office for test situation

definitions.meaning: the US president's office in the White House has an egg-shaped floor plan
a London cricket ground that hosts Test matches

explanation.surface: Someone compares the White House's layout with the venue for an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: THE OVAL is a London cricket ground that stages Test matches; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is the elliptical shape of the White House office; the second is the cricket venue in Kennington.

clue.text: Some are believed to oppose authority

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A group of people are supposedly about to resist those in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt or rise against those in power is to defy authority.

clue.text: Archaic version of, for example, this yarn

definitions.text: Archaic version of, for example, this
definitions.meaning: an old spelling of the word for a crossword hint, which is what this sentence is
a ball of thread or yarn

explanation.surface: A self-referential remark that this tale is an old-fashioned version of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yarn' suggests a story, but the sense here is thread wound into a ball, as in Theseus's thread in the labyrinth.
explanation.definitionFit: The old spelling of the word for a puzzle hint also names a ball of thread.

clue.text: Inhabitant of country using pin to secure silver

indicators.note: to secure means the first piece holds the second fast inside it

parts.note: a cotter is a pin or wedge that fastens parts of a machine
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A rural resident fastens some silver with a pin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'using' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural labourer living in a small country house is so called.

clue.text: Fastidious Welshman taking year to bind book collection

indicators.note: to bind means the Welshman and the year enclose the books between them

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name, short for David
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A fussy Welshman spends a year having a set of books bound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' is a link joining the Welshman to the year; 'to bind' has the pair wrap round the book collection. NT for New Testament is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone particular and fussy about food or manners is delicate in taste.

clue.text: Blankets, for a start, and cold sheet, possibly

definitions.text: Blankets, for a start, and cold sheet, possibly

indicators.note: for a start asks for the opening letter of the word Blankets
possibly signals the letters may be rearranged into another possible order

explanation.surface: Bedding consists of blankets to begin with and a chilly sheet, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds: B from 'Blankets' plus EDCLOTHES, the anagram of COLD SHEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Blankets and sheets are the coverings on a bed, which is what the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Asian church worker one's introduced

indicators.note: introduced means the pieces are brought into the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
an ant is the crossword's stock worker
the letters of one's, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A church employee from Asia has come in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introduced' places the worker and 'one's' inside the church abbreviation; 'Asian' looks like it describes the worker but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The language and people of Canton in southern China are Asian, so the word serves as an adjective or noun.

clue.text: Enchanting woman, good at spelling

definitions.meaning: a woman who casts enchantments, a witch
skilled at casting spells, punning on orthography

explanation.surface: A charming woman who is also a fine speller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spelling' looks like orthography but means casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch casts spells and enchants, so she fits both readings.

clue.text: Bring in closed vessel, say

indicators.note: say tells us the vessel's name is heard, not spelt, giving another word of the same sound

parts.note: an urn is a vessel, often lidded or closed

explanation.surface: Someone is told to carry in a lidded container.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring in money is to make it by working.

clue.text: Cut into shape when weight is redistributed

indicators.note: is redistributed means the named letter is taken out and placed elsewhere in the word

explanation.surface: Something is trimmed to form when its load is shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: W moves from the front of WHEN to third place.
explanation.definitionFit: Wood or stone chopped and shaped with an axe or chisel is described this way.

clue.text: Unexpected success, finally capturing king in revolt

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word success
capturing means the revolt takes the king inside it

parts.note: an uprising is a revolt
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A rebellion unexpectedly succeeds, ending with the king taken prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unforeseen catches you off guard, which is astonishing.

clue.text: Hooligan causing damage in funfair

indicators.note: damage done to the word wrecks its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A thug runs amok at a fairground.
explanation.definitionFit: A brute or thug is a violent troublemaker.

clue.text: Provide note about a gentleman at Windsor

indicators.note: about means the note is turned round

parts.note: fa is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
Master Ford is a gentleman in Shakespeare's The Merry Wives of Windsor

explanation.surface: Someone supplies a message about a man at Windsor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses FA to AF; 'a' is a link. Windsor suggests royalty, but the reference is Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: To supply or give something, as a view affords pleasure, is the sense.

clue.text: Imbibed, and ultimately had a row

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of the word had

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers or taxis

explanation.surface: Someone drank and in the end got into a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' tempts as a quarrel, but it means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To have swallowed liquid, especially alcohol, is to have consumed a drink.

clue.text: Paid advocate for information about reactions

parts.note: fee'd, given a fee, means paid
to back someone is to support or advocate them

explanation.surface: A hired lawyer is after details of how people responded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'advocate' looks like a lawyer but is the verb, to support.
explanation.definitionFit: Comments and responses to something done are gathered as information.

clue.text: Producers of notes, as accepted by consumer protection agency

indicators.note: accepted by means the second word is taken into the first

parts.note: BSI is the British Standards Institution, which sets standards protecting consumers
taken as written

explanation.surface: Banknote makers are approved by a watchdog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notes' suggests banknotes; it means musical notes. The BSI is the UK body behind the Kitemark safety standard.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep male singers, plural in the Italian form, produce low musical notes.

clue.text: It's serving in the place of a carpenter's appliance

definitions.meaning: a Latin-derived preposition meaning instead of
a bench clamp holding wood while it is worked

explanation.surface: A tool is acting as a stand-in for a carpenter's gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's' and 'a' are link words; the OCR stray full stop is not printed.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is instead of, as in a deputy's title; the second is the woodworker's gripping tool.

clue.text: Quick to reject bad article

indicators.note: to reject means the pieces are thrown back, read in reverse

parts.note: evil is bad
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone quickly refuses a poor piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reject' turns EVIL A round. 'Quick' means living, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in its old sense means living, as in the biblical phrase about judging the living and the dead.

clue.text: Delivered in Mediterranean port? Doesn't sound like it

definitions.text: Delivered in Mediterranean port? Doesn't sound like it

parts.words: Delivered in Mediterranean port? Doesn't sound like it
parts.note: the past tense of speak is spelt like the Egyptian port named after a pasha, though the port's name is pronounced differently

explanation.surface: Something is handed over at a Mediterranean harbour, but the name is pronounced otherwise.
explanation.walkthrough: Port Said in Egypt is spelt like the word for spoken but pronounced 'sah-EED'.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that are delivered aloud are spoken, and the Egyptian harbour shares the spelling.

clue.text: Aesop's kind — men disposed to express views bluntly

indicators.note: disposed means the letters are arranged afresh into a new order

parts.note: the letters of Aesop's, the S counted

explanation.surface: The fable-writer's sort of men are inclined to tell it straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses all of AESOPS KIND MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying frankly what you think is to state one's opinions without holding back.
